title: Marc Farag, Damian Harland and Dan Nixon — Bank capital and liquidity (Bank of England Quarterly Bulletin, 2013 Q3, pp. 201–215)
use: Historical UK central-bank conceptual primer for bank balance-sheet funding, equity versus deployable cash, valuation bases and high-level ratio denominators. Original chapter ledger, definitions, calculations and exercises supply their own assumptions.
verification: Opened official landing page dated 17 September 2013 and actual 15-page PDF. Read printed pp. 201–206 (balance-sheet assets/funding, loss absorption, capital/liquidity distinction, accounting and valuation box), liquidity discussion p. 207 and high-level ratio comparison p. 209. The 2013 incurred-loss timing, then-proposed accounting changes, deposit-protection limits and regulatory thresholds are deliberately excluded from current claims. No source numerical example is reproduced.

title: OCC, Federal Reserve, FDIC and NCUA — Interagency Policy Statement on Allowances for Credit Losses (United States, 1 June 2020; 85 FR 32991)
use: Dated US accounting-policy context for a loss valuation account, provision changes, write-offs against the related allowance, forward-looking information and scope limits. The chapter uses a stipulated simple positive-allowance ledger, not a complete CECL implementation or current compliance certification.
verification: FDIC live 2020 letter URL returned 403; official FDIC archive metadata and actual 14-page Federal Register PDF retrieved. Read scope on printed p. 32995 and overview of ACLs on p. 32996, including footnotes 10–11 on recoveries/possible negative allowances and write-off terminology, periodic provision adjustments and write-offs. The model intentionally excludes negative-allowance cases and off-balance-sheet accounting; no claim of universal nonnegative ACLs or complete current GAAP/regulatory application.

title: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision — Principles for Sound Liquidity Risk Management and Supervision (September 2008)
use: Historical international supervisory method context for timed cash obligations, operational/legal availability and avoiding reuse of encumbered collateral. Not a national-law definition, regulatory ratio calculation or claim that a central bank will lend.
verification: Old bcbs144.pdf route redirected to the official publication page dated 25 September 2008; followed its actual 44-page PDF. Read introduction/footnote 2 on printed p. 1 and principles 5–6 on p. 3 and 8–9, 12 on p. 4 covering cash horizons, transfer restrictions, intraday settlement, collateral location/encumbrance and unimpeded liquid assets. Source numbers, stresses and current implementation requirements are not imported.
